Our nurses and clinicians are the heart and soul of our healthcare system - they are always there for us, and I’m proud to stand in solidarity with them!

EWIB released a detailed economic report that confirms that the pipeline has made eastern Connecticut the highest region of employment growth in Connecticut from 2020-2025- by 33%. 

Since the program launched, over 6,400 trainees have been placed into jobs at over 670 employers.

The Manufacturing Pipeline Initiative is still expanding, and with the historic demand signal for submarine construction from the recently awarded $76.6 billion Navy contracts, I will continue to secure funding so the program reach even more young people and adult jobseekers in our region.

text:
Monday’s Northeast airport disruptions are a reminder that the United States’ transportation system depends on reliable, modern infrastructure.

Yet @SecDuffy is asking Congress for more money while the FAA has spent just 20% of the billions Congress already provided to modernize our air traffic control system and is well behind schedule. A recent Government Accountability Office report says the FAA still can’t clearly say how much the modernization will cost or when it will be finished.

While Duffy says we need to modernize infrastructure, he has called for eliminating the federal Mass Transit Account, which is a critical source of funding for public transportation.

You can’t claim to be fixing America’s transportation infrastructure while leaving modernization money on the table and cutting support for transit. We must invest in both.

quoted.text:
HERE'S WHAT HAPPENED:

Yesterday, a primary telecom switch failed. A backup line was accidentally cut by a NJ Transit construction crew. Flights in the Northeast ground to a halt.

Repairs were made as quickly as possible, and all operations in Northeast resumed by the afternoon. 

Why did it happen? Our digital infrastructure is still running on 40-50 YEAR OLD TECHNOLOGY.

We have made incredible progress in overhauling the air traffic control system, but Congress MUST give us the money to FINISH THE JOB.

Rumors that Chinese automaker BYD’s CEO will accompany President Xi Jinping to meet President Donald Trump in Washington this week have triggered warnings from U.S. Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., and a broad coalition of auto industry groups, who fear Trump may grant the world’s fifth-largest automaker access to the U.S. market in exchange for permission to build a U.S. assembly plant.

Doing so would allow the automaker to establish a beachhead in the second-largest auto market, threatening North American automakers, suppliers and dealers, the senator said in a social media video posted Sept 22.

“This is quite literally an attempt by Chinese companies to kind of get their foot in the door of the American market. It’s just step one,” Slotkin said. “What they really want is to be able to bring in their cars from China, assembled in China, and sell them in the United States. They’re licking their chops to be able to do that.”

text:
My grandparents came to this country from Mexico as children with little money, little formal education, and limited English. They worked hard, built a successful business, and sent all five of their daughters, including my mom, to college.

Now their grandson serves in the United States Congress.

That is the American Dream.

This Hispanic Heritage Month, I’m thinking about their story and the countless Latino families whose hard work, sacrifice, and determination have helped build this country. I’m also thinking about whether that same dream is still within reach for families today.

At a time when immigrants are too often treated as threats instead of neighbors, and families who came here searching for a better life are living in fear, we cannot lose sight of what has always made this country extraordinary.

My family’s story is uniquely American. Now more than ever, we need to fight to keep that promise alive for the next generation.

text:
Donald Trump and Xi Jinping will meet in Washington this week. It’s critical that President Trump use this moment to secure increased AI safety coordination on the shared risks that frontier models hold, while also confronting China’s calculated efforts to overtake the U.S. in the AI development race.

Frontier AI models are developing faster than experts ever believed possible, with safety risks that researchers, industry and governments alike agree could hold existential threats. We need formalized international coordination and communication — with China and other countries — to ensure the push to develop and diffuse the most capable AI models does not cause catastrophic consequences for humanity.

China also has a long record of stealing American technological advancements and intellectual property — including through distillation attacks in which Chinese AI labs train models on America’s advanced AI models and then use those increased capabilities to threaten our national security. Trump must hold Xi to account for this blatant theft. 

Finally, Trump should reverse course on selling advanced chips to China. These chips give us advantages in safety and computing power to outcompete China in AI development — and selling them to China only squanders the leverage and innovation advantage that we have developed here in the U.S. Since we are concerned that China will not pace its development of AI to ensure its safety, we should not be selling China the chips to make that prospect even more likely. If Trump refuses to withhold sensitive technology from China, I’m hopeful that Congress will.

We are in a moment of great technological transformation and upheaval. Federal inaction is not an option. The U.S. must seize this opportunity for international leadership in protecting against AI’s gravest risks.

Yesterday, when I heard Donald Trump address the UN and say "to the victor goes the spoils," I thought about my grandfather who served in World War II. 

Conquest for plunder was the logic of the adversaries the Greatest Generation defeated.

When World War II ended, America had every chance to take whatever it wanted from a broken world. 

Instead, we helped rebuild former enemies, wrote rules that applied to the strong and weak alike, and led the effort to create the UN so borders would no longer be redrawn by force.

That choice made us the world's most powerful and respected nation for 80 years. 

Americans of both parties built that order, from Truman and Eisenhower to Reagan. I want my kids and grandkids to inherit an America the world still trusts, one that leads by building partnerships and keeping its word. 

That is our America worth defending, and it is the legacy we owe the Greatest Generation. 

It's a legacy I'll never stop fighting for.
https://t.co/qpzRMMOO9O

There are common sense steps Congress can take to combat heat islands and protect Americans.

One of those is my TREES Act, which would plant millions of trees nationwide to combat heat waves and lower utility bills.

We discussed survivor benefits, casualty assistance, and support for families grieving a death by suicide.

When a servicemember dies, our responsibility to their family does not end. I will continue working to make sure military and veteran families have access to the benefits, services, and support they have earned.

If you or someone you know has lost a military loved one, TAPS is available 24/7 at 800-959-TAPS (8277).

text:
Since Sunday’s ICE-related shooting in Austin, TX, I immediately began working with my subcommittee to find answers as Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Homeland Security, including whether or not the agent involved was wearing body worn camera – technology I advocated for when finalizing the DHS appropriations bill for 2026.  

It is unfortunate that we are still awaiting that clarification from ICE given the recent public reporting that the shooting involves a new recruit and was not using a body camera, despite clear instruction and funding from Congress as well as prior confirmation from ICE that body cameras had been deployed to all ICE agents in Texas. We have also asked several questions about the agencies involved in this investigation and the role they will play, confirmation on whether the agent(s) involved will remain in Texas for the duration of the investigation as well as their current duty status, why Mr. Perez was moved to a detention facility with a bullet remaining in their body, and the future outlook of procuring dashboard cameras as well as justification for the prioritization of non-criminals for deportation.
 
I have been equally engaged in the on-camera assault on two U.S. citizen teenagers by ICE agents in Alamo, TX as well as the recent deportation of Teresa de Jesus Ochoa Briseno. We are awaiting further clarification from ICE on the events of that day and if and when the agent’s body worn camera footage may be released to Congress.

More than 20 people, including several American citizens and other people who are lawfully present in the United States and engaged in the legal immigration process, have been shot during rogue federal immigration enforcement operations since President Trump took office in 2025.

The recent shooting of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a DoorDash delivery driver, in Austin, Texas, during a violent ICE encounter is yet another cruel demonstration of how this agency is out of control and running roughshod over civil rights and due process.  Early reports indicate that the ICE agent was a recent recruit who failed or refused to utilize his body camera during the incident. Deeply troubling as well, Mr. Graces Perez continues to be denied proper medical care to remove the ICE agent’s bullet that remains lodged in his back.

I join with my @OversightDems colleagues to demand a full and independent investigation free from obstruction by the Trump Administration.  Congress must intervene to restrain and transform ICE to remove it from our communities, enforce body camera requirements, adopt reasonable use of force standards, and commit to other major reforms to hold it accountable to the American people. I will continue to withhold all ICE funding until this rogue agency complies with the law.

Today, the Russians launched a ballistic missile strike on Kyiv just as we were meeting with members of Congress and discussing the Lindsey Graham law and the need to strengthen sanctions. Russia will not end this war without pressure. As people were sleeping, flashes from explosions lit up the sky. Once again, the main targets of their strike were Kyiv and civilian infrastructure, residential buildings, a maternity hospital, energy infrastructure, and logistics. Two people have already been reported killed. My condolences to the family and loved ones. There are also people who have been injured. Emergency services are working – people are trapped in one of the buildings. The air raid threat persists in some regions of the country.

We discussed exactly how to protect against these threats with @RepBrianFitz, @RepMikeQuigley, @RepMarcyKaptur, @RepGolden, @RepJoeWilson, and @RepGregoryMeeks. Every such attack happens because the pressure on the aggressor has never become total, and Russia believes it can continue to bet on ballistic terror. Right now, the United States has an opportunity to respond strongly. We need ballistic missile interceptors to protect lives. Sanctions against Russia and those helping it make money must be implemented. I thank both parties for their readiness to help protect lives.
